findings: The missense box says the sickle cell change is 'A to T' and the text says 'T is substituted by A' (CTC to CAC); these describe the coding and template strands of the same change. The lesson and the diagram explain both, flagged.

The silent example 'GGC to GGU' is an mRNA codon change though described as a DNA code. The book says some PKU medicines contain synthetic PAH; the enzyme-substitution drug in use (pegvaliase) is a different enzyme, phenylalanine ammonia lyase. The lesson attributes the statement to the book, flagged.
The sequence in the original point-mutation diagram is an illustrative example, not a real gene; the diagram says so. The boxes on minor mutations, harmful mutations and treatments are carried.
